title: Will the Trump administration announce a suspension of habeas corpus before January 20, 2029?
description: In May 2025, Stephen Miller, a senior advisor in the Trump administration, stated that the administration was “actively looking at” suspending the writ of habeas corpus to facilitate deportations, citing the constitutional provision allowing suspension [<u>“in time of invasion”</u>](https://time.com/7284743/what-is-habeas-corpus-under-threat-suspension-trump-administration/). This consideration arises amidst the administration’s invocation of the 1798 Alien Enemies Act to expedite the deportation of individuals, particularly targeting members of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua. The use of this wartime law has led to legal challenges and scrutiny over due process rights. The Supreme Court blocked the administration's attempt to use the AEA for deportation, emphasizing the need for adequate notice and [<u>the opportunity to challenge such actions under habeas corpus rights.</u>](https://time.com/7286140/supreme-court-immigration-aliens-act/)
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 20, 2029, the executive branch announces it is suspending the writ of habeas corpus in any part of the United States.

Resolution will be based on an official proclamation, executive order, Department of Justice memorandum, or other formal government action explicitly suspending the writ of habeas corpus that is intended to have the force of law according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
fine_print:
* The writ of habeas corpus refers to the constitutional right of individuals to challenge the legality of their detention before a court.
* Failures to grant habeas corpus to specific individuals or opposition to legal actions invoking habeas corpus in specific court cases will not suffice. There must be a general and formal suspension of the right.
* Suspension of habeas corpus is not necessarily universal — for example, it may apply only to a specific group (e.g., non-citizens), a particular region (e.g., border areas), or under defined conditions (e.g., national security emergencies). Any such announced suspension would still result in a **Yes** resolution.
* This question resolves based on an executive branch announcement of a suspension of habeas corpus that is intended to have the force of law. Therefore, its actual implementation, including such scenarios as being enjoined by courts, is immaterial for resolution.

title: Will the US establish a government program rewarding information leading to deportations before January 3, 2027?
short_title: Will a government program reward deportation tips before 2027?
description:
Throughout US history, there have been various forms of civilian tip lines and enforcement incentives related to immigration, but none yet offering paid rewards. Currently, the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tip line allows civilians to report suspected immigration violations, but it does not offer monetary incentives. Given the ongoing debates about immigration policy and border enforcement, there is a possibility that certain states or the federal government could introduce a monetary reward system to encourage civilian participation in deportation efforts.

*This forecast question was created by Bright Line Watch, a nonpartisan watchdog group. Forecast on their other questions* [*here*](https://www.metaculus.com/c/brightlinewatch/)*.*
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 3, 2027, a United States federal or state government formally establishes a program that provides monetary rewards to civilians for providing information leading to the deportation of individuals from the US.

For this question to resolve as Yes:

* The program must be officially established by a federal executive branch department (e.g., DHS, ICE, DOJ), a state executive branch agency, or a federal or state legislature through enacted legislation.
* The program must offer monetary compensation or financial incentives in exchange for providing information that contributes to the deportation of undocumented immigrants or individuals otherwise subject to removal proceedings.
* The program must become active before January 1, 2027.

This question will not resolve as Yes if:

* There is no monetary reward involved (e.g., a general tip line or anonymous reporting system without financial compensation).
* The program is proposed or debated but not officially established and implemented before the deadline.
* The program is created only by a private organization rather than a government entity.
* The monetary rewards are only offered to law enforcement officers or government employees, rather than civilians.

title: Will the US Dollar Index (DXY) drop below an average of 88 for any 90-day period before the 2029 presidential inauguration?
short_title: Will DXY’s 90-day average fall below 88 before Jan 20, 2029?
description:
The [US Dollar Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Dollar_Index) ticker symbol DXY and nicknamed the Dixie, is a weighted geometric mean of the US dollar (USD) compared with the following six currencies according to the Intercontinental Exchange ([pdf](https://www.ice.com/publicdocs/ICE_USDX_Brochure.pdf)) which maintains the index: 

* Euro 57.6%
* Japanese Yen 13.6%
* British Pound 11.9%
* Canadian Dollar 9.1%
* Swedish Krona 4.2%
* Swiss Franc 3.6%

The index began in 1973 and included a basket of European currencies that got consolidated into the Euro in 1999. The DXY's starting value in 1973 was 100, and subsequent changes in its value reflect its changes relative to that baseline. [According to Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/u/usdx.asp):

> An index value of 120 suggests that the U.S. dollar has appreciated 20% versus the basket of currencies over a particular time period. Simply put, if the USDX goes up, that means the U.S. dollar is getting stronger in value compared to the other currencies.

> Similarly, an index value of 80, indicating a fall of 20 from its initial value, implies a 20% depreciation in strength relative to the other currencies. The appreciation and depreciation results are a factor of the time period in question.

Over history, the DXY has fluctuated as follows, ranging from an all-time high of almost 165 in 1984 and an all time low of nearly 70 in 2007:

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/USDX_Blue-d93b4f708867472dba7a05f3b3f2fa0b.webp)

In April 2025, in the days following President Donald Trump's [Rose Garden announcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_Day_tariffs) of potential high tariffs and trade wars, the USD [fell](https://www.morningstar.com/markets/dollar-hits-3-year-low-against-euro-tariff-turmoil) against other major currencies, hitting a 10-year low against the Swiss franc and a 3-year low against the Euro. This fall was a surprise to many observers, with the tariffs [having been expected](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/04/06/trumps-tariffs-were-expected-to-boost-the-dollar-but-theyre-not.html) to boost the dollar. 

According to an analysis by [BNP Parabas](https://economic-research.bnpparibas.com/html/en-US/Could-Trump-drive-down-dollar-1/21/2025,51217): 

> Donald Trump’s position on the greenback is somewhat ambivalent and contradictory, straddled between maintaining its dominance and wanting to see it depreciate to boost the competitiveness of US exports. The
resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if at any point after the launch of this question and before January 20, 2029, the value of the US Dollar Index (DXY) averaged over any 90-day period is is less than 88.00, according to  [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/DX-Y.NYB/history/).
fine_print:
The 90-day period refers to calendar days rather than trading days and will be the arithmetic mean of the daily Close prices for DXY. For example, at the time of this question, the 90-day period January 25, 2025 through April 25, 2025 encompassed 63 trading days presented by Yahoo Finance and had an average daily Close value of 104.51.

Should the resolution source be at a different location, fail to exist at the time of resolution, or have clearly erroneous data, Metaculus may choose another appropriate resolution source.

The question may, at Metaculus' discretion, resolve as **No** before January 20, 2029 if it becomes mathematically impossible for the 90-day average through January 20, 2029 to be less than 88.00.

title: Will the size of the US Supreme Court increase before 2029?
short_title: Will the size of the US Supreme Court increase during Trump's second term?
resolution_criteria: If before January 1, 2029, [28 U.S. Code § 1](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/1) is amended to specify that the Supreme Court of the United States shall consist of greater than a total of 9 justices, then this question resolves as **Yes**. Otherwise it resolves as **No**.
fine_print:
Any change in the law must take effect on or before 1 Jan 2029; a law that goes into effect after this will not be sufficient, even if it has been enacted earlier.

This question will not consider the number of judges serving. Seats being vacant for any reason (including never being filled) will have no impact on this question.

This question resolves based on law that has been enacted: that is, passed by both Houses of Congress and received presidential signature, or via veto override.

This question will resolve based upon the time in Washington, D.C., which is the Eastern Time Zone of the US.

title: What percent of US GDP will come from manufacturing in the first half of 2028?
short_title: What percent of US GDP will come from manufacturing in the first half of 2028?
description:
One of the most fundamental patterns in economic development is the progression from agriculture and resource extraction to industry to services. In this [three-stage model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-sector_model), countries typically begin relying on primary activities, such as agriculture, mining, forestry, and fishing, then transition toward manufacturing and industrial production as productivity gains free up labor. In the final stage, mature economies pivot toward services. In the original model by Fisher, Clark, and Fourastié, these services were thought of as the transport, distribution and sale of goods, but later reconceptualisations of the model expanded the definition to include finance, healthcare, education, and entertainment.

This trend has become a particular concern for some US policymakers, with the GDP share of manufacturing dropping by more than a third from 1997 (16.1%) to 2021 (10.5%). At the same time the GDP share of manufacturing in the world dropped by less than 15 percent (from 19.0% to 16.5%).

<iframe src="https://data.worldbank.org/share/widget?indicators=NV.IND.MANF.ZS&locations=US-1W" width="600" height="450" frameborder="0" scrolling="no"></iframe>  
Declining manufacturing will likely have a negative impact on the US economy with [13 million workers](https://www.nist.gov/blogs/manufacturing-innovation-blog/manufacturing-america-contributing-our-economy-employment-and) employed in manufacturing jobs, and a large part of research and innovation being spearheaded by manufacturing companies. Indeed, some states would be [disproportionately affected](https://www.epi.org/publication/the-manufacturing-footprint-and-the-importance-of-u-s-manufacturing-jobs/#epi-toc-9) by manufacturing losses. Weak manufacturing would also lead to greater reliance on other countries and is thus often viewed as a [national security issue](https://www.cnas.org/publications/commentary/its-time-for-a-true-industrial-strategy-for-american-national-security); although [not everyone agrees](https://www.cato.org/publications/policy-analysis/manufactured-crisis-deindustrialization-free-markets-national-security#).

For these reasons, Trump [pledged](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/24/us/politics/trump-economic-policy.html) during his campaign that he would implement policies to increase the manufacturing capacity of the US. These included the early 2025 tariffs, but also other actions, such as the [removal of regulatory barriers](https://
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the average manufacturing share of GDP for Q1 and Q2, 2028, reported in the FRED series [Value Added by Industry: Manufacturing as a Percentage of GDP](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/VAPGDPMA) (VAPGDPMA).
fine_print: This question will resolve after both values have been published by FRED and when they are first accessed by Metaculus. Later revisions will not impact resolution.

title: Will the US government order the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) or NASDAQ to be closed before January 20, 2029?
short_title: Trump closes NYSE or NASDAQ before January 20, 2029?
description:
The [New York Stock Exchange](https://www.nyse.com/index) (NYSE) and the [National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations](https://www.nasdaq.com) (Nasdaq) are the two largest stock exchanges in the world by market capitalization, ranked 1st and 2nd respectively.

Both stock exchanges run year round, closing only on weekends and on recognized holidays such as Christmas Day and New Years day; or during National Days of Mourning, like when the late President Jimmy Carter passed away; or for extended periods of time in more exceptional circumstances such as:

* World Wars 1 and 2.
* Great Depression Banking Crisis.
* September 11 Attacks.

The historical precedent for the above closures were to stabilize the markets by preventing large sell-offs and to stem panic. They have typically been executed in coordination with the US government, rather than a Presidential order for example.

President Donald Trump, during both his first term and ongoing second term, has been a frequent commenter on the stock market and its governing institutions. Trump has [publicly called](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-04-23/powell-attempts-balancing-act-as-trump-tests-fed-s-autonomy) for current Chairman Jerome Powell to lower interest rates, something many observe as an infringement of the Federal Reserve's autonomy. Indeed, Trump has also had internal discussions on having [Powell removed](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/04/23/business/trump-jerome-powell/index.html), which would be an unprecedented decision with no clear legal basis and something his closest advisors strongly advised against<sup>1</sup>. Trump has also [attacked](https://x.com/TrumpDailyPosts/status/1834712936952349040) the SEC and the Nasdaq after halting trading of [Trump Media & Technology Group Corp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Media_%26_Technology_Group) (\$DJT), a company majority-owned by Trump, due to volatility - a very normal procedure for any stock:

> Why is NASDAQ halting the sale of DJT? What right do they have to do this? \[...] Are they taking orders from the SEC, which, for political reasons, delayed us for an inordinate amount of time, therefore hurting the stock very badly? I am going to hold NASDAQ, and maybe the SEC, liable for doing what they are doing.

Moreover, Trump has often [linked](https://x.com/TrumpDailyPosts/status/1752035267274518696) stock market performance to government performance and success, but, in light of his tariff campaign, the st
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 20, 2029, the US government orders the [New York Stock Exchange](https://www.nyse.com/index) (NYSE) or the [National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations](https://www.nasdaq.com) (Nasdaq) stock markets to be closed for one or more entire regularly-scheduled trading days.
fine_print:
Note that stock market closures ordered for the following reasons will **not** be sufficient to resolve the question to **Yes**:

* National Days of Mourning.
* National Holidays.
* Natural Disasters (e.g., hurricanes, volcanic eruptions etc.)

Closures due to other reasons would be sufficient.

Requests or pressure to close made by the government but without a formal order (for example, see the [1914 closure of the NYSE](https://elischolar.library.yale.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1346\&context=journal-of-financial-crises)) do **not** count.

Whether an order is followed and subsequent challenges to the legality of such an order are immaterial, the question immediately will resolve when a qualifying order is made.
